title: PM Modi Flags Off Chennai Metro Phase 2, Cutting Poonamallee–Vadapalani Trip to 30 Minutes
excerpt: The 14.6-km Yellow Line section — Phase 2's first operational stretch — connects the western suburbs to the metro network with fares from ₹10 and peak trains every 10 minutes.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. PM Modi and CM Joseph Vijay inaugurated the Poonamallee Bypass–Vadapalani stretch of Chennai Metro Phase 2 on October 11, and both leaders rode the inaugural train.
  • The 14.6-km Corridor 4 (Yellow Line) section, built at a cost of about ₹4,900 crore, cuts the Poonamallee–Vadapalani commute from 60-90 minutes by road to around 30-40 minutes by metro.
  • Trains will run from 7 am to 9 pm at 10-minute peak intervals; fares range from ₹10 to ₹40, with ₹50 for through journeys to the airport, Central or Egmore via interchange at Vadapalani.
  • Diaspora visitors arriving in Chennai can use the new line to reach Porur and the western suburbs: trains opened to passengers on October 11 after the inauguration, running 4 pm to 9 pm on day one.

Phase 2's first stretch goes live

Six years after work began, Chennai Metro Rail's Phase 2 network has its first operational section. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee Bypass–Vadapalani stretch on Sunday, with Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay joining him to flag off services — both leaders among the first commuters on the new line. The 14.6-kilometre elevated section is part of Corridor 4, the Yellow Line, which will eventually extend 26.1 kilometres to Lighthouse near Marina Beach.

https://x.com/narendramodi/status/2109222516807934146

"The 14.6-km Corridor 4 (Yellow Line) section, built at a cost of about ₹4,900 crore, cuts the Poonamallee–Vadapalani commute from 60-90 minutes by road to around 30-40 minutes by metro."

The inauguration was one of several projects the Prime Minister dedicated during his Chennai visit, spanning metro rail, highways, railways and ports — with drone bans and 'Red Zones' declared around Meenambakkam, Guindy, Porur and Nandambakkam during the visit.

What opens, and what comes next

Eleven stations are initially served from Poonamallee Bypass toward Vadapalani, including Poonamallee, Karayanchavadi, Kumananchavadi, Kattupakkam, Iyyappanthangal, Thelliyaragaram, Porur Bypass and Porur Junction. Six stations on the double-decker section between Porur Junction and Vadapalani — Alapakkam, Karambakkam, Valasaravakkam, Alwarthirunagar, Saligramam and Avichi School — are being bypassed for now as construction continues; an opening date for those stops has not been confirmed.

CMRL will run 15 trains at 10-minute intervals during peak hours (8 to 11 am and 5 to 8 pm), with initial operating hours of 7 am to 9 pm. On opening day, passenger service ran from 4 pm to 9 pm after the inauguration program concluded. The Phase 2 trains carry new features: charging points, half-height platform screen doors at elevated stations, and digital route maps. Driverless operations will wait until mid-2027, officials said. The Commissioner of Metro Railway Safety approved the section in February, with relaxations granted in May, clearing the way for today's launch.

The commuter math

The practical difference is stark. The Poonamallee–Vadapalani road trip — through bottlenecks, narrow bypasses and industrial freight traffic — takes up to 90 minutes at peak hours. The metro does it in about 30 to 40 minutes. At ₹10 to ₹40 a ride, and ₹50 for through journeys to Chennai Airport, Central or Egmore via the Vadapalani interchange to Phase 1, the new line also plugs the western suburbs and the Chennai–Sriperumbudur industrial corridor into the wider network. A paid-to-paid skywalk at Vadapalani, currently under construction, will smooth the interchange.

The opening also unlocks a larger transit shift: the ₹150-crore Kuthambakkam bus terminus near Thirumazhisai, about 6.5 km from the Poonamallee Bypass station, had been waiting on this metro link. Once the section is running, the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority plans to move long-route buses to Bengaluru, Hosur, Vellore and Krishnagiri from CMBT Koyambedu to Kuthambakkam, with MTC shuttle services connecting the metro stop to the depot.

Diaspora angle

For NRIs landing in Chennai — whether visiting family in the western suburbs or heading to the Sriperumbudur industrial belt — the line gives a predictable, air-conditioned alternative to the city's traffic. Interchange at Vadapalani connects directly to the airport and Central station, and at ₹50 all-in, it is also the cheapest ride in town. Route, fare and timing details are available via Native Planet's Phase 2 guide and NowLivo's station-by-station breakdown.

What's next

Corridor 4's remaining construction toward Lighthouse continues, along with the rest of the 118-kilometre Phase 2 program. The skipped stations on the Porur–Vadapalani leg, driverless operations by mid-2027, and the Kuthambakkam bus integration are the milestones to watch. See also South Politics' inauguration report.
